operating_notes.text: FY26 revenue from contracts with customers was ₹39.15 Cr, of which ₹38.05 Cr came from within India.
The ₹1,840 Cr priority review voucher was recognised as other operating revenue under Ind AS 20.
Contingent liabilities were ₹84.74 Cr, including ₹51.90 Cr service-tax and ₹32.84 Cr income-tax disputed demands.
Q1FY27 revenue included ₹29.21 Cr from the terminated CMS Bridging DMCC licence after a USD 2 million (₹1,889 lakh) refund.
The USFDA priority review voucher for Sezaby was sold on April 30, 2026 for USD 195 million.
The company has a single reportable segment, Pharmaceutical Research and Development.

CESTAT Mumbai upheld SPARC's Order-in-Appeal dated 27.04.2018, confirming entitlement to a ₹27.51 Cr refund of accumulated CENVAT credit plus consequential interest; the Revenue's appeal was dismissed.

holders.name: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Key Employees Benefit Trust

timeline.summary: FY26 annual report shows a ₹1,553 Cr consolidated profit driven by a ₹1,840 Cr USFDA priority review voucher, an unmodified audit, and a ₹600 Cr promoter warrant issue.
Q1FY27 consolidated revenue was ₹39.9 Cr, including ₹29.21 Cr from the terminated CMS Bridging DMCC licence, and the net loss narrowed to ₹20.78 Cr from ₹51.87 Cr a year ago.
SPARC held its 21st AGM on August 10, 2026; all resolutions passed including appointment of Anil Raghavan as MD & CEO and retirement of Dr. Rajamannar Thennati.
On 13 August 2026, SPARC applied to stock exchanges for reclassification from Promoter Group to Public category under Regulation 31A, with approval still pending.
On 4 October 2026, SPARC said CESTAT Mumbai upheld its 2018 Order-in-Appeal and dismissed the Revenue's appeal, confirming its entitlement to a ₹27.51 Cr CENVAT credit refund with interest.
